design.concept: Decision-first board for the manager: on entry a single highlight shows how many team expenses wait for a decision, and under it a grid of cards, one per pending expense. Each card is readable in one glance (who, amount, date, category, resubmission) and carries its main action, so the common case is one click to the analysis page.
design.decisions: Followed the decisionFirst template: the collection is a grid of cards (3 columns wide, 2 narrower), never a table, and each card opens with a full-width status strip, coloured with the status tokens and holding the status words. A resubmission after a correction is added to the strip text. The detail overlay and in-panel outcome row of the template do not apply here: the page declares no decision command, and the only intent is navigating to the team-expenses page, where the person analyses and decides. The page also holds no state to remember an open card. So the 'Analisar e decidir' button sits on the card, where the action comes before any reading, and no scene host is needed (single view). The metric card leads the page because the intent is to make the pending volume noticeable. Valor and dates are shown from the row fields (date formatted with Intl, amount shown as delivered). Loading shows skeleton cards, error shows the message above a retry button, and empty shows a large icon, one sentence and a refresh action (the only main action available without an expense id). 'Carregar mais' appends the next page when the list says it has more.
